sections.html:
Grand Junction is the county seat of Mesa County and the biggest city in Colorado outside the Front Range corridor, 247 miles west-southwest of Denver. It serves as the hub of the Western Slope. The 2020 census counted 65,560 people, and the 2025 estimate is 71,780.

Colorado Mesa University brings students and staff to town, and owners of rentals near campus are one group that sometimes decides to sell. Buyers also compare city houses with homes in nearby Palisade, Fruita, Loma and the Redlands, so expect that comparison when you talk price.

This is a cold semi-arid climate with about 9 inches of precipitation a year, so roofs and exteriors take more sun than rain.

  • July averages 78.2 degrees F and January averages 27.4.
  • About 68 days a year reach 90 degrees or higher, and about 8 reach 100 or higher.
  • The average last freeze falls on April 25 and the first on October 11.

Long hot spells wear down air conditioners, roofing and exterior paint. A retail buyer's inspector often zeroes in on the cooling system and the roof. A cash buyer prices whatever turns up and does not ask you to repair it first, which is useful if your cooling system is old.

Anyone running a short-term rental inside city limits needs a license from the City of Grand Junction, renewed every year under Ordinance No. 5163, adopted July 5, 2023. The application fee is $275 per property. The city also caps how many residentially zoned lots may hold a primary short-term rental.

  • Downtown (North Ave to I-70B, Highway 50 to N 17th St): no more than 7 percent of residentially zoned lots.
  • Outside downtown: no more than 3 percent.
  • Lots with four or fewer units: one primary and one secondary rental allowed.
  • Lots with five or more units: no more than 10 percent of units.

If your house has been used this way, check that the license is current before you talk to a buyer, since the caps decide who can get a new one. Community Development is at 250 N 5th Street, phone 970-244-1430. Ask them whether a license passes to a new owner, because that answer affects what a buyer will pay.

DateWhat happens
January 1Property is valued as of this date
January 31Treasurer mails tax bills
February 28First installment due
April 30Full-year payment due
May 1Real property valuation notices mailed
June 8Last day to file a real property protest
June 15Second installment due

The calendar repeats each year. A sale between January and the payment dates can leave the prior year's tax unpaid, and the title company will want to see that balance before closing.

Valuation notices go out May 1, and a protest must be filed by June 8. If you are thinking about selling soon, read the notice anyway. A lower value can trim a buyer's tax bill, and it shows you are watching the paperwork.

An unpaid tax bill will not stop a sale. Call the Mesa County Treasurer for the parcel's balance and pass the number along to your title company. At the table, that amount and any mortgage payoff are subtracted from what the buyer pays. Because every deduction shows on a single statement, your net is known before your pen touches paper.

Colorado attaches a documentary fee to recorded deeds: a penny for each $100 of the price, with leftover fractions counted as a whole hundred. It is paid at the clerk and recorder's office. Deals of $500 or less skip it. The contract decides which side pays.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Grand Junction
sections.html:
Give us the address and describe the condition. We review it and extend an offer that you are free to accept or refuse. If you accept, a title company verifies who owns the property, orders the tax certificate and drafts the deed, which is then recorded in Mesa County.

With no bank involved, the calendar is set by the title work and by your preferred date. Price and timing stay open until we have seen the house.

The sequence runs call, visit, written offer, title work, signing. At the signing the title company walks through the numbers, clears taxes and any loan, and pays you what is left.

Dig out your newest tax statement and the phone number of your mortgage servicer. A house that once hosted short-term guests needs its city license papers too. Gather receipts for the roof and the cooling system in particular, because heat does the most damage in this valley. Jot down any tenants and whether they plan to stay.

A cash buyer accepts the house with its flaws. That means no repair haggling after an inspection and no waiting on a lender's appraiser, two of the biggest sources of delay in a conventional listing. Showings also disappear, which matters if you live in the house or if tenants do.

sections.h2: Who sells quickly in this market
sections.html: Those who call tend to be landlords near campus, owners of former vacation rentals that cannot get a license, heirs with an estate to settle, and homeowners facing a roof or cooling bill they would rather skip. Requesting an offer is free. Set it next to a realistic listing outcome after repairs, fees and months of waiting, and go with the better fit.

sections.h2: Selling a house that was a short-term rental
sections.html:
Buyers of a former vacation rental want to know three things: whether the license was ever valid, whether it can continue after the sale, and whether the lot sits inside a capped zone. Have the answers in writing from Community Development before you set a price. If the license cannot continue, the house is worth what it is as a regular home or long-term rental, and a buyer who plans the same use will adjust the offer accordingly.

An investor who buys for cash can look at those facts quickly, without waiting on a lender's rules about rental income, and decide on the spot.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the tax calendar
sections.html: Plan your closing with the payment dates in mind. A closing in the weeks after bills go out means the title company will be working with a freshly issued statement. A closing near the April 30 or June 15 deadlines means you may be asked to pay a due installment from the proceeds. Neither is a problem, but knowing which situation you are in keeps the closing statement free of surprises.

faqs.q: What county is Grand Junction in?
faqs.a: Mesa County. Grand Junction is the county seat, so the Mesa County Treasurer bills property taxes and deeds are recorded in Mesa County.

faqs.q: When is the second property tax payment due in Mesa County?
faqs.a: June 15. The first installment is due February 28, and full payment is due April 30.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Grand Junction house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires an annual short-term rental license with a $275 application fee per property, and it caps the share of residential lots that can have a primary short-term rental.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Grand Junction house without repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not have to fix the roof, cooling system or cosmetic items first. The offer reflects the condition.

faqs.q: How hot does Grand Junction get?
faqs.a: About 68 days a year reach 90 degrees F or higher, and about 8 reach 100 or higher. That heat is why inspectors look closely at cooling systems and roofs.
